# Latent growth curves

A latent growth curve model is a special case of a ctsem model. Its
process changes at a constant rate, with no random fluctuation, and
people differ in where they start and how fast they grow. This article
fits a linear growth curve, then two growth processes with several
indicators, then lets the measurement error depend on the level of the
process.

``` r

library(ctsem)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Data

Thirty people, each observed eight times at irregular times. Each person
has their own intercept and slope, and people who start higher grow more
slowly:

``` r

set.seed(3)
nsubjects <- 30
nobs <- 8
intercept <- rnorm(nsubjects, 3, 2)
slope <- rnorm(nsubjects, 0.45, 0.15) - intercept * 0.05
dat <- expand.grid(obs = 1:nobs, id = 1:nsubjects)
dat$time <- dat$obs + runif(nrow(dat), -0.5, 0.5)
dat$eta1 <- intercept[dat$id] + slope[dat$id] * dat$time
dat$y1 <- dat$eta1 + rnorm(nrow(dat), 0, 0.2)
dat <- dat[, c('id', 'time', 'y1', 'eta1')]
head(dat)
#>   id     time       y1     eta1
#> 1  1 1.216853 1.787250 1.722631
#> 2  1 2.322188 2.132112 2.309882
#> 3  1 3.320742 2.919136 2.840400
#> 4  1 3.699945 3.089174 3.041866
#> 5  1 5.101135 3.700201 3.786300
#> 6  1 5.929836 4.116992 4.226578
```

`eta1` is the true value, which a real data set would not have. It is
kept here to compare with the estimates.

``` r

ggplot(dat, aes(time, y1, colour = factor(id))) +
  geom_point() + geom_line(aes(y = eta1)) +
  theme_bw() + guides(colour = 'none')
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Linear growth

The default ctsem model is more flexible than linear growth, so a few
matrices change:

- `DRIFT = 0`: the rate of change does not depend on the current level;
- `DIFFUSION = 0`: the process does not fluctuate, so change is
  deterministic;
- `CINT = 'slope'`: the continuous time intercept is the constant rate
  of change, the slope;
- `MANIFESTMEANS = 0`: the starting level `T0MEANS` takes the place of
  the intercept.

By default the free intercepts, here the starting level and the slope,
vary over people and are correlated. Since the observation times differ
within and between people, the model is in continuous time. In discrete
time with an interval of one unit, a linear growth curve is the same
model.

``` r

model <- ctModel(type = 'ct',
  manifestNames = 'y1', latentNames = 'eta1',
  LAMBDA = 1,
  DRIFT = 0,
  DIFFUSION = 0,
  CINT = 'slope',
  MANIFESTMEANS = 0)
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

``` r

fit <- ctFit(dat, model, cores = 2)
s <- summary(fit)
s$popmeans
#>           mean    sd  2.5%   50% 97.5%  mode
#> T0m_eta1 2.926 0.274 2.392 2.936 3.424 2.927
#> mvary1   0.207 0.011 0.186 0.207 0.230 0.207
#> slope    0.321 0.028 0.269 0.323 0.376 0.322
```

`T0m_eta1` is the average level at each person’s first observation, and
`slope` the average slope. `popsd` gives their standard deviations over
people, and `rawpopcorr` their correlation:

``` r

s$popsd
#>           mean    sd  2.5%   50% 97.5%  mode
#> T0m_eta1 1.521 0.199 1.178 1.509 1.940 1.516
#> slope    0.147 0.020 0.112 0.147 0.193 0.147
s$rawpopcorr
#>                   mean    sd   2.5%   50% 97.5%   mode      z
#> slope__T0m_eta1 -0.236 0.171 -0.548 -0.24  0.12 -0.243 -1.381
```

The true values for these thirty people, which the estimates should be
close to:

``` r

first <- dat[!duplicated(dat$id), ]
c(start_mean = mean(first$eta1), slope_mean = mean(slope),
  start_sd = sd(first$eta1), slope_sd = sd(slope),
  correlation = cor(first$eta1, slope))
#>  start_mean  slope_mean    start_sd    slope_sd correlation 
#>   2.8948018   0.3275297   1.5681417   0.1591997  -0.2722724
```

[`ctPredict()`](https://cdriveraus.github.io/ctsem/reference/ctPredict.md)
shows the predictions for a few people. The predicted values (`yprior`)
use each person’s earlier observations only. Before the first
observation the prediction is the population average, and with each
observation the person’s own starting level and slope are learned:

``` r

ctPredict(fit, subjects = 1:3, timestep = 0.1, plot = TRUE,
  kalmanvec = c('y', 'yprior'))
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The smoothed values (`ysmooth`) use all of each person’s observations:

``` r

ctPredict(fit, subjects = 1:3, timestep = 0.1, plot = TRUE,
  kalmanvec = c('y', 'ysmooth'))
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Two processes and several indicators

A second process, `eta2`, has its own starting levels, related to those
of `eta1`, and declines by 0.2 per unit of time on average. It is
measured by two variables: `y2`, and `y3` with a loading of 0.8 and an
intercept of 3.

``` r

intercept2 <- 1 + 0.5 * intercept + rnorm(nsubjects, 0, 1)
slope2 <- rnorm(nsubjects, -0.2, 0.1)
dat$eta2 <- intercept2[dat$id] + slope2[dat$id] * dat$time
dat$y2 <- dat$eta2 + rnorm(nrow(dat), 0, 0.5)
dat$y3 <- 3 + 0.8 * dat$eta2 + rnorm(nrow(dat), 0, 0.3)
```

In the model each process has a starting level and a slope. `y2` has a
loading of 1 and an intercept of 0, which set the scale of `eta2`, and
`y3` gets a free loading and a free intercept. The intercept is the same
for everyone, which `indvarying = FALSE` in its string says.

``` r

model2 <- ctModel(type = 'ct',
  manifestNames = c('y1', 'y2', 'y3'),
  latentNames = c('eta1', 'eta2'),
  DRIFT = 0,
  DIFFUSION = 0,
  CINT = c('slope1', 'slope2'),
  T0MEANS = c('int1', 'int2'),
  MANIFESTMEANS = c(0, 0, 'manintercept3, indvarying = FALSE'),
  LAMBDA = c(
    1, 0,
    0, 1,
    0, 'lambda3'))
```

[`ctModelLatex()`](https://cdriveraus.github.io/ctsem/reference/ctModelLatex.md)
shows the structure:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

``` r

fit2 <- ctFit(dat, model2, cores = 2)
summary(fit2)$popmeans
#>                 mean    sd   2.5%    50%  97.5%   mode
#> int1           2.927 0.277  2.391  2.921  3.464  2.928
#> int2           1.977 0.261  1.493  1.967  2.483  1.969
#> lambda3        0.801 0.020  0.760  0.801  0.841  0.802
#> mvary1         0.207 0.011  0.187  0.206  0.230  0.207
#> mvary2         0.504 0.024  0.457  0.504  0.552  0.504
#> mvary3         0.305 0.016  0.275  0.305  0.337  0.304
#> manintercept3  2.943 0.040  2.864  2.942  3.022  2.941
#> slope1         0.321 0.027  0.268  0.321  0.374  0.322
#> slope2        -0.205 0.021 -0.248 -0.205 -0.165 -0.206
```

The slopes come out close to the generating 0.27 and -0.2, and the
loading and intercept of `y3` close to 0.8 and 3.

``` r

ctPredict(fit2, subjects = 1:2, timestep = 0.1, plot = TRUE,
  kalmanvec = c('y', 'ysmooth'))
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Measurement error that depends on the level

A measurement instrument may work better for some values of the process
than for others. Here the measurement error of `y1` grows with the level
of `eta1`:

``` r

dat$y1 <- dat$eta1 + rnorm(nrow(dat), 0, log1p_exp(0.8 * dat$eta1 - 3))
ggplot(dat, aes(eta1, log1p_exp(0.8 * eta1 - 3))) + geom_line() +
  labs(y = 'measurement error sd of y1') + theme_bw()
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The measurement error cell of the model becomes an expression in the
latent process.
[`log1p_exp()`](https://cdriveraus.github.io/ctsem/reference/log1p_exp.md)
keeps the standard deviation positive. Free parameters inside an
expression are declared in `PARS`:

``` r

model3 <- ctModel(type = 'ct',
  manifestNames = 'y1', latentNames = 'eta1',
  LAMBDA = 1,
  DRIFT = 0,
  DIFFUSION = 0,
  CINT = 'slope',
  MANIFESTMEANS = 0,
  MANIFESTVAR = 'log1p_exp(errorsd_intercept + errorsd_byeta1 * eta1)',
  PARS = c('errorsd_intercept', 'errorsd_byeta1'))
fit3 <- ctFit(dat, model3, cores = 2)
summary(fit3)$popmeans
#>                     mean    sd   2.5%    50%  97.5%   mode
#> T0m_eta1           2.874 0.270  2.332  2.875  3.397  2.867
#> slope              0.347 0.043  0.262  0.349  0.428  0.347
#> errorsd_intercept -2.909 0.188 -3.247 -2.907 -2.563 -2.904
#> errorsd_byeta1     0.780 0.054  0.678  0.781  0.886  0.779
```

The generating values were -3 for the intercept and 0.8 for the effect
of `eta1`. The band around each smoothed trajectory includes the
measurement error, which is much smaller for person 4, whose level is
lower:

``` r

ctPredict(fit3, subjects = c(3, 4), timestep = 0.1, plot = TRUE,
  kalmanvec = c('y', 'ysmooth'))
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

[`vignette('measurement-models')`](https://cdriveraus.github.io/ctsem/articles/measurement-models.md)
has more on measurement that depends on the state, including loadings.
